items.appliesWhen: You name the type explicitly, e.g. in a variable or a helper that builds the messages object. Calling toast.promise(p, {...}) inline needs no change - T is inferred.
items.pitfall: The parameter defaults to unknown, so an un-parameterised annotation still compiles - and still hands your success callback `unknown`, which is the defect. Passing the type is what fixes it, not the compile.
items.verify: A success callback receives the resolved value with its real type: toast.promise(loadOrder(), { success: (order) => `Saved #${order.id}` }) compiles without a cast.
items.note: promise<T> declared a type parameter and then threw it away, because the messages interface hardcoded unknown. Every call site that wanted the resolved value had to cast.
items.action: Annotate as ToastPromiseMessages<T> where you name the type; inline object literals need no change.

items.appliesWhen: You render <ds-toast> yourself and bind message. ToastService callers pass body already and change nothing.
items.pitfall: An unknown input on a component is a template error under strictTemplates, but a plain attribute is not - message="…" without brackets keeps compiling and silently renders an empty toast.
items.verify: A hand-placed <ds-toast [body]="…"> renders its text; nothing in your templates still binds message on ds-toast.
items.note: ToastOptions and ToastEntry always called the text body; only the component input said message, so one concept had two names either side of the same service.
items.action: Rename the ds-toast input from message to body.

items.appliesWhen: You set any of the five anywhere - :root, a theme file, or a per-instance ds-toast block.
items.pitfall: The old name simply stops resolving, and the declaration it sits in is dropped whole - so a toast loses its border rather than falling back to a default. Nothing errors.
items.verify: A :root override of --ds-toast-border-color repaints the toast border, and no rule in your styles still names --ds-toast-border.
items.note: They are colours, and every other border token in the library already carries -color. These five were the last holdouts of the pre-rename naming.
items.action: Add -color after -border in all five token names.

items.appliesWhen: You rely on a ds-banner or ds-alert being announced by a screen reader when it appears. A banner that is page furniture needs no change - silence is now the correct behaviour for it.
items.pitfall: Nothing breaks visibly and no build fails, so a regression here is invisible without a screen reader: an app that raised an error banner in response to a request and relied on the alert firing now shows it silently.
items.verify: A banner your app raises in response to an event carries announce and is spoken; a static strip carries none and is silent on route change.
items.restore: Pass [announce]="true" to get the previous behaviour on a given instance.
items.note: An alert region fires on insertion, so a statically-placed strip interrupted the reader on every client-side route into its page - 12 such regions on this library's own docs. MDN advises against alert on content the user has not interacted with, and the DS convention is that a new capability is off by default.
items.action: Add [announce]="true" to any ds-banner or ds-alert that should be announced when it appears.

informational: Typing on a closed ds-select now commits the type-ahead jump, as a native <select> does. The path existed but was unreachable, so nothing that worked before changes. NO ACTION.
A chip row's guard against a parent that hugs its content was unreachable and is removed; the measurement is unchanged. NO ACTION.

ToastService now shows at most 5 toasts at once by default, where it was previously unlimited. Extras queue and appear as earlier ones dismiss, so nothing is lost. Set DS_TOAST_CONFIG maxVisible to any other number, or 0 for no cap. The stack also animates when a toast is added rather than jumping; --ds-toast-shift-duration and --ds-toast-shift-easing tune that.

Toast announcements moved off the visual toast and onto the CDK LiveAnnouncer, so info, success and loading toasts are now announced at all — previously only error and warning were, and only by luck. Nothing to change if you use ToastService. If you render <ds-toast> directly it no longer carries role or aria-live and is silent to a screen reader: that markup is a specimen, and anything that should be announced should go through the service.
